name: milp_binary_indicator
steps: Define integer variables: t (trucks), a (airplanes), b (boats), n (trains), all >= 0.
Define binary indicator variables: m_t=1 if t>0, m_a=1 if a>0, m_b=1 if b>0, m_n=1 if n>0.
Link quantity to indicator via big-M: t <= M*m_t, t >= m_t (small positive), similarly for a, b, n. M = min(resource_upper_bound / resource_per_unit) ≈ 74 for trucks (wood), 41 for trains (steel).
Wood constraint: 12*t + 20*a + 15*b + 10*n <= 890.
Steel constraint: 6*t + 3*a + 5*b + 4*n <= 500.
Truck-train mutual exclusion: m_t + m_n <= 1 (if trucks, no trains).
Boat requires airplane: m_b <= m_a (if boats>0, airplanes>0).
Boats <= trains: b <= n.
Maximize: 5*t + 10*a + 8*b + 7*n.
Solve with HiGHS, integer variables for t,a,b,n; binary for m_t,m_a,m_b,m_n.

name: milp_bigM_direct
steps: Use 4 integer production variables: t, a, b, n >= 0.
Use 4 binary indicator variables: y_t, y_a, y_b, y_n (1 if corresponding product is made).
Big-M linking: t <= 100*y_t, a <= 100*y_a, b <= 100*y_b, n <= 100*y_n.
Resource wood: 12*t + 20*a + 15*b + 10*n <= 890.
Resource steel: 6*t + 3*a + 5*b + 4*n <= 500.
Conditional truck-train: y_t + y_n <= 1.
Conditional boat-airplane: y_b <= y_a.
Boat count <= train count: b <= n.
Objective: maximize 5*t + 10*a + 8*b + 7*n.
Same model structure, different big-M values (100) and no minimum quantity enforcement.

name: milp_indicator_tightened
steps: Integer variables: t, a, b, n >= 0.
Binary indicators: m_t, m_a, m_b, m_n.

Tightened big-M: truck max from wood: t <= 74; from steel: t <= 83; so M_truck = 74. Train max: n <= 89 (wood), n <= 125 (steel) -> M_train = 89. Airplane max: a <= 44 (wood), a <= 166 (steel) -> M_a = 44. Boat max: b <= 59 (wood), b <= 100 (steel) -> M_b = 59.
Link: t <= M_truck*m_t, a <= M_a*m_a, b <= M_b*m_b, n <= M_train*m_n.
Mutual exclusion: m_t + m_n <= 1.
Boat needs airplane: m_b <= m_a.
Boats <= trains: b <= n.
Maximize: 5*t + 10*a + 8*b + 7*n.
